tools.name: dns_lookup
tools.description: DNS records of a domain over DNS-over-HTTPS (Cloudflare, with Google Public DNS as fallback): A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SOA, CAA, or all of them. Returns each record with its TTL, the resolver used, the DMARC record and DNSSEC status. The full report is at report_url (/dns?name=<name> on iplover.

tools.name: verify_bot
tools.description: Is a request really from the crawler it claims to be (Googlebot, Bingbot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot...)? Give the address, the user agent, or both. The address is checked against the operator's published IP lists and, where the operator supports it, forward-confirmed reverse DNS under the operator's domain.

tools.name: check_my_ip
tools.description: The public IP address this MCP request came from, with Cloudflare's approximate location and network for it. For a remote agent this is usually the agent platform's address, not the end user's device. The full report is at report_url (/ip/<address> on iplover.com).

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check_domain · Private data: dns_lookup · Public sink: lookup_ip, check_domain, verify_bot.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check_domain · Private data: dns_lookup · Public sink: lookup_ip, check_domain, verify_bot

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
